### StandardAero Renews DGAC Chile Certification, Strengthening MRO Support for South America


StandardAero has renewed its recognition as a Foreign Repair Station by the Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil (DGAC) of Chile, maintaining its CMAE No. E-133 certification.


The renewal reinforces StandardAero’s ability to support customers operating Chilean registered aircraft and components, while further strengthening the company’s international maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) network.


CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)


### The DGAC Chile Recognition Includes Capabilities covering:


- **Airframe maintenance for Airbus and Bell helicopters (line & depot-level):**
Airbus AS350/EC130, AS355, AS332, AS365, EC120 and EC135 series
Bell 205, 206, 212/214 and 407 series
- **Dynamic components MRO (line & depot-level) for Airbus helicopters:** MGB, TGB, Bevel, Epicyclic, among others for AS350, EC130/H130, AS355 helicopters.
- **Avionics: Radio systems, instruments, etc.**
Modification, repair, testing and overhaul
- **Structural repairs (line & depot-level) and modifications**
Including composite, sheet metal, tubular and wooden structures
- **Non-destructive testing**
Including liquid penetrant and magnetic particle inspection


The renewed recognition continues a relationship with DGAC Chile that dates back to 2006 and is valid through to July, 2028.


The renewal of CMAE No. E-133 further strengthens StandardAero’s ability to support customers with trusted MRO capabilities across borders.

**StandardAero** is a leading independent pure-play provider of aerospace engine aftermarket services for fixed- and rotary-wing aircraft, serving the commercial, military and business aviation end markets. StandardAero provides a comprehensive suite of critical, value-added aftermarket solutions, including engine maintenance, repair and overhaul, engine component repair, on-wing and field service support, asset management and engineering solutions. StandardAero is an NYSE listed company under the ticker symbol SARO.
